blindSummary:
The clearest enacted modern local anti-LGBT rule outside one neighbouring state/province: a 2024 city-level regulation in this state/province prescribes, under two penalty provisions, oral and written warnings, cessation of activities, social-rehabilitation programmes, and administrative fines of roughly one million units of local currency targeting LGBT people. A further district-level authority in this state/province finalised a draft local regulation on public tranquillity containing an explicit LGBT prohibition with administrative fines and "rehabilitation" for people of same-sex attraction. Academic analysis notes implementation remains weak precisely because rehabilitation facilities do not exist. This state/province also appears in an international LGBT-rights organisation's eight-state/province analysis of discriminatory local rules.

This sits below the country-wide average because an enacted local rule with specified sanctions creates visitor-facing risk (detention, forced rehabilitation programmes, fines) that does not exist in most states/provinces. However, the documented absence of enforcement infrastructure and no recorded arrest or caning keep it above a neighbouring state/province where patterned mob violence with zero accountability is the primary threat, and above the country-wide floor where no such local rule exists at all.
